correctness.rationale: The Hilbert coordinate \(\psi_K(x)=\tfrac12\log((x-a)/(b-x))\) is an isometry from \((a,b)\) to the real line, and \(G\) becomes a closed coordinate interval of length \(D_H\). For an ordered convexified-separated sequence on a line, each new point outside the convex hull of its predecessors must extend the running span by at least \(\alpha\), so at most \(\lfloor D_H/\alpha\rfloor+1\) points occur; a monotone equally spaced sequence attains this bound, proving equality with ordinary packing. Direct cross-ratio algebra shows the polar interval pair has the same Hilbert diameter. Arya--Mount Lemma 4.3 then becomes the claimed fully convexified square because ordinary and convexified factors coincide and monotonicity absorbs the \(\eta/2\) factor into \(\eta/4\). Fresh numerical cross-ratio checks on several asymmetric nested interval pairs independently reproduced exact primal--polar equality.

final_claim: For every nested pair of nondegenerate real intervals \(G=[c,d]\subset(a,b)=\operatorname{int}K\) and every \(\alpha>0\), ordinary and convexified Hilbert packing numbers coincide exactly and equal \(\lfloor D_H/\alpha\rfloor+1\), where \(D_H=\tfrac12\log\!\frac{(d-a)(b-c)}{(c-a)(b-d)}\). The same value is preserved under reversed polarity. Consequently Arya--Mount's fully convexified diagonal-product bound holds in dimension one as \(\widehat M_{\mathrm{diag},H}(K^\circ,G^\circ;\eta)\le \widehat M_H(K^\circ,G^\circ;\eta/4)^2\), with multiplicative constant one.
limitations: Only one-dimensional Hilbert geometry (nested real intervals) is resolved.
The constants do not settle Arya--Mount Problem 5.1 in higher dimensions.
